reverse_engineering.FortiOS: The PowerShell literal is byte-for-byte the raw FortiOS chain and is piped into & ssh admin@firewall.example. Both stop miglogd and syslogd, clear crash logs, and use traversal auto-script names to write setup code and Apache mod_md configuration. Node code downloads pM.js, runs Node with that same saved path, then removes it on child close. Nested downloads write index.js, index.wasm, ipssem.js and lldprx; a 180000ms timer then launches Node with the staged paths. The second traversal write configures a Node DNS-01 hook, remote CA directory and always-renew mode, supporting recurring activation. No source obfuscation is present beyond short variables and concatenated paths.
reverse_engineering.npm: Original SHA-256 verified; archive contains exactly index.js, test.js and package.json, identical to supplied extraction. preinstall runs node test.js with stdout and stderr redirected to null. test.js reads hostname, home directory and username; a helper converts UTF-8 bytes to hex and passes each into a hostname assembled inside getNetworkDownloadSpeedData. checkDownloadSpeed chooses an HTTP client by URL.protocol and calls get on that URL. Three GET first labels recover the three identities. Network-interface addresses are calculated but never sent; uptime collection and send are comments. index.js exports a normal download/upload benchmark; its upload method generates random bytes and sends JSON through caller-provided options, and is not invoked by test.js.
reverse_engineering.replay: QuickJS ran the original Node setup text and both original npm JavaScript files with only in-memory HTTP/filesystem/process/OS/timer stubs. Recorded five FortiOS GETs, five file writes, first launch and close cleanup, 180-second timer, second launch; npm recorded exactly three GETs carrying synthetic reviewer, review-host and /home/reviewer. No real command or HTTP request was performed.
reverse_engineering.limits: Appliance version, vulnerable deployment, authorization, actual network/exploit success and remote payload contents are unavailable. The firewall.example target suggests template/redacted context but does not make the logging blackout and traversal-based payload staging ordinary administration. OAST use could be security research; no authorized install-time identity-collection context is supplied. Verdicts rest on the bundled actions, not an external feed, family attribution or successful delivery.
